header: CONSUME: append the objects in `entries`, in array order, to MANIFEST.json `rounds[]` (they are drafted at indices 48..65, second element of this file). Do not append this header.

PROVENANCE: every status below is copied from the live gate run `python3 .ufo/waves/round-12/closure-check.py` (exit 1, debt=16 contradictions=0 unrowed_terminated=9 pending_round=8) unless the evidence section of that row says otherwise; the gate's own suggested status and the drafted status agree for all 16 debt rows. `rounds[]` indices referenced by `supersedes.entry` are the pre-append indices (0..47) and stay stable because `rounds` is append-only.

GROUPING RULE: one object per flagged row for `closure-correction` entries (each correction names the entry that carries the row it replaces, and every `supersedes` carries `entry` per the protocol pin); one object per round key for a first-time entry (`type: closure`, rounds 1, 2, 16, 17, 18), which carries every one of that round's rows in its `lanes` map - the partial-entry shape entry #45 used. Row-to-entry map, in file order: kake r15, kumitate r15, kagi r15, kotoba r15, protocol r15 (all supersede #45), protocol r14 and kengaku r14 (supersede #27), protocol r13 (supersedes #44), kengaku r13 (supersedes #21), kengaku r12 (supersedes #38), aggregator r11 (supersedes #14), aggregator r10 (supersedes #13), aggregator r9 (supersedes #43), kama r1 (new round-1 entry), kama r2 (new round-2 entry), round-16 entry (kasegi failed, kake ok, kumitate ok, kotoba ok, kagi ok), round-17 entry (kasegi ok; kake, kumitate, kotoba, kagi in-flight), round-18 entry (kasegi in-flight). No (lane, round) pair appears twice, so last-wins is unambiguous.

MARKER PREDICATE: the six `failed` rows below are the lane-rounds whose contract-path file is a contentless completion marker. Predicate applied (P:150-155, the gate's `_grade_file`): bytes < 400 AND no hex run >= 7 AND no `SHONEN` heading. Measured: round-13/protocol.md 275 B hex=0 SHONEN=0; round-14/protocol.md 340 B hex=0 SHONEN=0; round-10/aggregator.md 187 B hex=0 SHONEN=0; round-12/kengaku.md 274 B hex=0 SHONEN=0; round-15/kotoba.md 273 B hex=0 SHONEN=0; round-16/kasegi.md 273 B hex=0 SHONEN=0 (`grep -oE '(^|[^0-9a-fA-F])[0-9a-f]{7,}([^0-9a-fA-F]|$)' <file> | wc -l`, `grep -cE '^#{1,6}[[:space:]]*SHONEN' <file>`, `stat -c%s <file>`). Marker => `failed` whatever the lane actually did, and the marker file is kept as a conformance defect.

JUDGMENT 1 - the two protocol self-gradings: `protocol r13` and `protocol r14` are this lane's own lane-rounds, graded by this lane (integrator-of-record), so the round notes must disclose self-grading. Both grades are mechanical, not discretionary: the files are markers by the measured predicate above, which prescribes `failed`; the log lines (`launch`/`complete`) are independent of the grader. Round-13's own draft (rounds[44]) recorded protocol r13 in-flight at closed_at 2026-09-28T22:23:00-03:00, before its complete line existed - the in-flight row was true when written and is corrected here, not falsified in place. protocol r14 rides #27, whose not-dispatched row was true at its closed_at (2026-09-28T20:55:00-03:00) and was superseded by dispatch evidence 4h20m later; the row is written as `failed`, not `not-dispatched`, because the lane-round terminated with a marker.

JUDGMENT 2 - why kengaku r13, kasegi r17 and the kake rows stay `ok` although they cite no resolvable commit: the protocol has two grade layers. A filed report with defects is `ok` + conformance defect (P:150-155 'A short report naming a real committed round-work hash is a defective report, not a marker: status ok, minimum-content defect recorded'; step 1: 'A report violating the report contract (missing heading, dead or orphaned hash, report filed before its commit) ... is a conformance defect in the round notes - it does not change the lane's status unless the round's rules already prescribe failed'). `failed` is prescribed only by the marker sentence ('no changes, no evidence pointer, no resolvable commit') or by the absence of a report. Each file below is >= 400 B, is tracked, and carries evidence pointers (paths, commands, line cites) - so it is a defective report, not a marker. Mechanically the opposite grade is also impossible to write: the gate raises `failed-vs-report` (a contradiction, not debt) for a `failed` row whose non-marker report was on disk at/before closed_at. The alternative reading of this round's brief (ok stands only if the report names a resolvable commit) is therefore recorded as a defect on each such row rather than as a status change, and is flagged here for L1 arbitration.

JUDGMENT 3 - every ok row below records its report path, byte count, introducing main-repo commit, SHONEN count, and sampled cited-hash ancestry. The round-15 gate searches main, the six child repos, kama-shokunin, and the operator-owned read-only trees including `~/Projects/origin-work/open-bug-bounties`. That last root was added after the first draft: token 1307b8b in kasegi r17 now resolves as the open-bug-bounties HEAD/ancestor, so the draft-time `dead` quote in that row's notes is superseded by this judgment and is not a status defect. Missing headings, operator/sweep attribution, and unresolved citations remain conformance defects; a real tracked report remains ok unless it satisfies the marker predicate.

JUDGMENT 4 - attribution defects recorded, not repaired: history is never rewritten, so the row notes name them. Reports landed by the fleet-relaunch commit 17c1fadfddc5ecbfa5ef362ef44d111792fa3e94 (Joao Pedro Veiga, 2026-09-29T00:19:02-03:00, subject `fleet relaunch: all L1 lanes -> @m_swe; repo moved to ~/Projects/shokunin; kama row; pending protocol+scorecard edits`): protocol r13, kengaku r12, kengaku r13, kasegi r16, kasegi r17, kagi r16. Reports landed under the operator identity rather than the lane identity (<lane>-shokunin / <lane>@shokunin.local): kake r15 (3069841), kake r16 (c3b0c0e), kumitate r15 (4d518fe, subject says 'recovered'), kumitate r16 (5846679), kagi r15 (3485880), kotoba r16 (208db49), kama r1 (74768ab). Integrator-identity marker commits: protocol r14 (ef36757), aggregator r10 (f5d8507). Clean lane identity: aggregator r9 (cc6d9d4 aggregator-shokunin) and kotoba r15 (4419fb9 kotoba-shokunin, a marker committed by the lane).

JUDGMENT 5 - the closed_at instant bounds the nine in-flight rows. 'No lane may be recorded in-flight unless its mission was live at closed_at' (P:241-249). All nine were live at the probe instant 2026-09-29T00:33:48-03:00 (verified: no matching complete line, each counter equaled N, and no contract-path report existed), so every entry uses 2026-09-29T00:34:00-03:00. Age alone does not create closure debt: an aged open mission remains a compliant live in-flight row and appears only in the informational stale-mission probe. A later complete line or landed report creates stale_in_flight debt and triggers the next correction pass; round 15 performed that follow-up at 01:27:10.

JUDGMENT 6 - kama is in the lane universe without a roster row. `MANIFEST.json` roster ids = kasegi, kengaku, kake, kumitate, kotoba, kagi (no kama); `rounds[36]` (round 11.5, type `mint`) holds the probation record ('kama-shokunin minted in probation ... Roster row withheld until >=3 verified self-iteration rounds per the new clause; lane wired into watchdog'). Driver evidence: `scripts/shokunin-watchdog.sh:14` LANES="protocol aggregator kasegi kengaku kake kumitate kotoba kagi kama", `:24` `[kama]="$SK/kama-shokunin"`, state `.ufo/state/kama.round` -> 2. So the kama lane-rounds are legal (lane universe = roster UNION base lanes UNION driver counters) while the roster row and the ROADMAP.md table row are pending operator-side per Lifecycle - the ROADMAP.md line that names kama is still the watchlist bullet ('Integrator decision pending: mint or record a rejection in the round notes'), i.e. stale against rounds[36]. GATE CONSEQUENCE, measured both ways: the round-12 gate's LANES constant omits kama (`.ufo/waves/round-12/closure-check.py:47`, likewise `.ufo/waves/round-13/closure-check.r13.py:57`) and its `_roster()` = LANES UNION roster ids, so it reports `unknown-lane` for these two rows; the round-15 gate (`.ufo/waves/round-15/closure-check.py`) widens the lane universe to MANIFEST `roster` UNION base LANES UNION `.ufo/state/*.round` basenames UNION lanes named by a dispatch/complete/wrap line UNION lanes named by a prompt file, and GateExecutor measured on this very draft that `kama 1 ok` (ledger row 61) and `kama 2 in-flight` (row 62) grade normally with zero `unknown_lane` findings. So no gate or roster edit is needed for these two rows: the r12-gate finding was purely its hardcoded LANES and is a closed issue, not L1 work.

VERIFICATION (historical, run, not asserted). A scratch root appended these 18 objects at `closed_at` 2026-09-29T00:34:00-03:00 over the 48-entry manifest. The round-12 gate returned debt=2 / contradictions=2 solely for kama r1/r2 because its hardcoded eight-lane universe omitted kama; a throwaway LANES amendment returned debt=0. An independent run with the round-15 gate admitted kama normally (`kama 1 ok`, `kama 2 in-flight`, zero unknown_lane); its only debt was `history_pin_unverifiable` because the scratch root was outside the anchored git worktree. Those ephemeral stdout captures were not retained. Durable replay is provided by `frozen/r15-pre-003400` (the bounded pre-append closure debt) and `frozen/r15-post-012710` (the final 74-entry ledger); both pin all stored inputs in `expected.json`. Recorded consequence: this draft needs no roster change to append, and round-15's dynamic lane universe closes the r12 gate's kama blind spot.

JUDGMENT 7 - surfaces examined this round and why they are not entry notes. (a) `.ufo/history-pin.json` pins entries 0-47 (k=48, sha256 ce97497ed699a8f0939be062d042cf4d6e3e7531116fbe4681593991d67f0a8e, manifest_commit ae19fca, pinned 2026-09-28T22:56:28-03:00 by 'protocol lane round-13 closure pass'); appends never invalidate it and regenerating it is a separate committed act (P §Round-robin step 4) - out of scope for this draft. (b) `.ufo/watchdog-driver.log` is 0 bytes and untracked; `grep -n 'watchdog-driver' scripts/shokunin-watchdog.sh` -> no output, so the committed driver does not write it; [INFERENCE] it is an empty artifact left by the relaunch's redirect, and it carries no evidence - no note cites it. (c) `.ufo/watchdog.log` carries 22 `wrap <lane> round=N complete; NOT respawning (fleet-wrap)` lines (a third verb). The round-12 gate's RE_COMPLETE matched only `complete <lane> round=N`, so a lane-round whose only termination line were a wrap line would have read live - named to the gate owner, and now adopted: the round-15 gate treats `wrap <lane> round=N complete; NOT respawning (fleet-wrap)` as termination evidence (P:224-231), pinned by its fixture `wrap-terminated-unreported` (completes 104 -> 126 = 104 `complete` + 22 wrap), and GateExecutor reports the live verdict unchanged by that widening, so no status in this draft is re-graded. Either way no row below rests on a wrap line alone: each is corroborated by a `complete` line or by the lane's counter. (d) The nine live rounds' prompts are untracked (`git status --porcelain`: `?? .ufo/prompts/<lane>-round-<N>.md` for protocol 15, aggregator 11, kasegi 18, kengaku 14, kake 17, kumitate 17, kotoba 17, kagi 17, kama 2) - non-durable dispatch evidence until committed with the round's integration commit (integrator scope); the dispatch lines exist, so the rows are in-flight regardless.

JUDGMENT 8 - dates. Every appended entry carries `date: 2026-09-29` (the append instant) while each `supersedes` triple carries the superseded entry's own date 2026-09-28; `closed_at` is present on every entry because every entry carries an in-flight row or a supersede-worthy row, and no entry carries a `not-dispatched` row, so no `lane_rounds` map is required (the two that are included annotate the lane's own counter where the round key alone would not).
